header.userPrompt:
Implement GitHub issue #79 in AlexITC/expense-tracker: warn on semantic duplicate bank statements at draft confirm time (account date-range overlap, implausible period length, period sanity), surfaced at confirm and as a badge on the statements list, warn-not-block. Full spec follows.

## Problem

The same bank statement can be imported twice as two separate statements, producing duplicate expenses that nothing detects.

Observed case: the same monthly statement for one account was imported twice under two different filenames. Both covered the identical period and had the identical set of rows, yet they imported as two distinct statements linked to two distinct documents with two distinct sha256 hashes.

Why it slipped through: dedup today is byte-level only (sha256 of the file), enforced in `CreateBankStatementDraftAction` and by the `document_user_sha256_unique` and `bank_statement_document_id_uq` constraints. A re-exported or re-downloaded PDF of the same statement has different bytes, so a different sha256, so none of those fire. The duplicate is semantic, not byte-identical.

The resulting duplicate expenses are also invisible to the existing expense dedup UI, because both sides are row-linked (the detector only pairs a row-linked expense with a non-row one).

## Goal

Add a semantic duplicate guard for bank statements. Warn the user, never hard-block. Getting explicit confirmation to proceed is the bar.

## Phase 1 (this issue)

At draft confirm time (`ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`, where a ready draft becomes a statement and the extracted metadata already exists), run these checks and, if any trip, return a warning the UI shows in a confirm dialog that the user can explicitly accept:

1. **Date-range overlap on the same account.** Compare the incoming `[period_start, period_end]` against existing statements for the same account, scoped by `(bank_name, product_type, account_last4, currency)` (there is no account entity). Warn on any range overlap, not just an equal period, so re-imports whose extracted dates drifted still trip it.
2. **Implausible period length.** Warn when `period_end - period_start` is not roughly one month (about 26 to 35 days). Covers a clean calendar month and a cycle like the 3rd to the 2nd.
3. **Period sanity (cheap, same warn path).** Warn when `period_start > period_end`, or when `period_end` is in the future.

Rules are warnings only. Nothing blocks the import; the user confirms and proceeds.

**Also surface the overlap check (rule 1) as a badge on the statements list page**, so pre-existing duplicates (like the case above) are visible without re-importing. Same query, second entry point.

## Out of scope (possible follow-ups)

- **Row-fingerprint match**: warn when the incoming row set (date + amount + description) substantially matches an existing statement's, even when the extracted periods differ. This is the strongest semantic signal and the true "dedup per content", but needs the parsed rows and a similarity threshold. Add only if period overlap proves insufficient.
- Gap / missing-month detection. That is a completeness feature, not dedup.
- A frontend sha256 pre-check. It compares bytes, so it would pass this case exactly like the backend did. Not worth building.

## Notes for the fix

- All user-owned queries must be scoped by `user_id`.
- Do not add a DB UNIQUE constraint on the metadata columns: they come from AI extraction and vary slightly between runs, so a hard constraint would be fragile. Keep it a confirm-time warning.
- Cleanup of an existing duplicate statement is separate: deleting the duplicate statement leaves its expenses row-less. Note those orphans have no receipt, so the current expense dedup UI does not surface them (see the dedup-flow improvement issue); that gap is tracked separately.
